Step 1 – look at the single mutants  
g1 → 75 % resistance  
g2 → 0 % resistance  
g3 → 50 % resistance  

Loss of G2 abolishes resistance completely, while loss of G1 or G3 only weakens it.  
Therefore the g2 phenotype is the most severe.

Step 2 – look at the double mutants  
g1 g2 → 0 % (same as g2)  
g2 g3 → 0 % (same as g2)  
g1 g3 → 10 % (far below either single mutant)

Whenever the g2 allele is present, the double mutant shows the g2 single-mutant phenotype (0 %).  
Thus the g2 mutation masks the effect of mutations in the other genes – G2 is epistatic to both G1 and G3.

Step 3 – interpret the pathway  
In a linear (biosynthetic/defence) pathway the epistatic gene is usually the downstream component.  
Hence G2 most probably acts downstream of the others, while G1 must act upstream – consistent with G1 being the transcription factor that regulates part of the pathway.  
Because the g1 and g3 single mutants still retain considerable resistance but the double mutant drops to only 10 %, G1 and G3 clearly act in different, partially overlapping branches (no full redundancy); nothing in the data demands them to be redundant – they just contribute to the same trait, which is a form of pleiotropy.

Step 4 – match with the options  
Only option (A) recognises that  
• G2 is epistatic towards G1, and  
• G1 is the transcription factor.

Options (B), (C) and (D) assign epistasis to the wrong gene.

Therefore the best answer is option (A).

Answer: A
